articles.headline: Liverpool win as new-arrival Jacquet makes 'step forward'
articles.description: Andoni Iraola heaped praise on defender Jeremy Jacquet after his impressive performance in Liverpool's 1-0 victory over AFC Bournemouth at the Vitality Stadium on Sunday.
articles.body:
Andoni Iraola heaped praise on defender Jérémy Jacquet after his impressive performance in Liverpool's 1-0 victory over AFC Bournemouth at the Vitality Stadium on Sunday.

Jacquet, who this week earned his first senior call-up for France, was the standout performer as Liverpool moved up to sixth in the table, helping them to keep three consecutive Premier League clean sheets for the first time since the start of the 2024-25 season.

"I'm happy for him because he's also received his first international call-up," Iraola said of the 21-year-old in his postmatch news conference. "He's going with France and that is a big national team and I know that he is happy. He's still very young, he is adapting really well to the Premier League.

"I think in the first games, physically he was feeling the change of rhythm, he was finishing with cramps, finishing really tired and we had to sub him. Today has been a step forward. He looked solid until the end and I think he's finished physically also in a good place. I hope he can continue this development."

Liverpool were not at their best against Bournemouth, but secured the three points through a second-half strike from Alexander Isak. It was the Sweden international's fourth league goal of the season -- a higher tally than he managed in the entirety of last term.

"The striker's job is like this," Iraola said. "He had a couple of crosses that he doesn't hit properly, one chance [he couldn't] control and this. I think he has to help us to be closer to the box, to play in the opposition half, to have meaningful possession and then, if the team is playing there, he will receive the rewards in terms of goals."

Reflecting on Liverpool's unbeaten start to the season, Iraola added: "I think overall we've improved, definitely since the first games. Some of the things we still need to improve, more things. I am happy it is the third clean sheet in a row in the league. Today is a kind of difficult game, I knew you never play comfortably here. Bournemouth don't allow you to play comfortably normally, they put you under pressure and you have to adapt and you have to win this kind of game.

"But we still have to get ready because the schedule that we have now, it's very difficult. I think we are playing against top-four teams and then in between Champions [League] and then in between Chelsea in the Carabao [Cup] and everything in two, three days.

"So we have to get ready because this next month, after this break, it's going be very demanding for us."

articles.headline: José Mourinho blasts ref, VAR: 'Two clear red cards' for Atlético Madrid
articles.description: José Mourinho blasted the referee and the VAR after Real Madrid's 2-1 derby defeat to Atlético Madrid, saying Atlético should have received "two clear red cards."
articles.body:
José Mourinho blasted the referee and the VAR after Real Madrid's 2-1 derby defeat to Atlético Madrid, saying Atlético should have received "two clear red cards" and claiming the on-field official "couldn't cope with the pressure."

Alejandro Grimaldo put Atlético ahead with a second-half penalty at the Metropolitano -- after defender Dean Huijsen was sent off for bringing down Giuliano Simeone -- before Jonathan David made it 2-0. Antonio Rüdiger pulled a late goal back as Madrid dropped to fourth in the LaLiga table.

However, Mourinho's postmatch news conference focused on two first-half incidents, when Atlético's Cristian Romero was shown a yellow card -- not a red -- for treading on Jude Bellingham's knee, while Lee Kang-in escaped punishment for a crunching challenge on Federico Valverde.

Mourinho brought printed-out photos of the two incidents into the press room to show journalists, before delivering a long, damning indictment of referee Miguel Ángel Ortiz Arias and VAR Daniel Trujillo Suárez.

"The story of the game is here," Mourinho said, holding up the images of the two challenges. "They're two clear red cards. With the difficulties we had afterwards -- with 11 versus 10 [players] -- you could imagine what it would have been like [for us] for 50 minutes with 11 versus nine.

"It's the CTA [the referee's committee]. It's all been very strange. It's a referee [Ortiz Arias] who, at 41, doesn't have international experience. I don't know why he was the referee. The poor guy came here and couldn't cope with the pressure.

"But for [the VAR] there's no pressure, at [RFEF HQ] Las Rozas there's no pressure. Or maybe there is and we don't know. ... That combination -- a poor referee, who's only done small games, and a VAR with a big history. Congratulations to the CTA."

The Portuguese coach said he hadn't yet seen a replay of Huijsen's red card and went on to list a series of incidents in games involving Real Madrid, Barcelona and Atlético in recent weeks, suggesting Real's rivals had benefitted.

"The penalty at Real Sociedad [for Atlético] is laughable," Mourinho said. "The penalty for Barcelona is laughable, the non-sending off [for Barcelona] against Athletic Club. So many things together. ... I thought I'd find a different league to the one I left [in 2013], and people told me no, and they explained why. But we'll fight."

Madrid are now six points behind leaders Barcelona with seven games played, going into the international break.

"If 'they' leave us in peace, and let us compete on an even playing field, there's a long way left," Mourinho said, when asked if his team could still fight for the title.

"I don't want to say this was prepared. I want to think they're mistakes, like a coach makes mistakes. I want to think the CTA made a mistake, and picked a referee of 41, who's never been in this situation. They made a mistake, that's all."

articles.headline: Patriots starting RG Mike Onwenu carted off with ankle injury
articles.description: Patriots starting right guard Mike Onwenu was carted off the field with an ankle injury late in the first quarter of Sunday's game against the Steelers.
articles.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- New England Patriots starting right guard Mike Onwenu was carted off the field late in the first quarter of Sunday's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and the team quickly ruled him out with a right ankle injury.

The injury came on a play when quarterback Drake Maye was sacked, and Steelers linebacker T.J. Watt landed on the back of Onwenu's legs.

In addition to Onwenu, starting outside linebacker Dre'Mont Jones left the game in the second quarter with a shoulder injury. After initially announcing Jones' return as questionable, the Patriots officially ruled Jones out early in the third quarter.

Onwenu is a seven-year veteran who has the longest tenure with the Patriots after being selected in the sixth round of the 2020 draft.

Durability has been one of his calling cards, as Sunday marked his 100th career regular-season game and 92nd start. A University of Michigan alum, he also has played in five playoff games (four starts).

Onwenu, 28, is in the final year of his contract in 2026.

Veteran Greg Van Roten, whom the Patriots signed to a one-year, $3 million deal on Aug. 18, took over for Onwenu.

articles.headline: Rangers place pitcher Cal Quantrill on 15-day injured list
articles.description: The Rangers put versatile right-hander Cal Quantrill on the 15-day injured list Sunday, a day after he exited following four batters and 12 pitches because of right lat tightness.
articles.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- The American League West-leading Texas Rangers put versatile right-hander Cal Quantrill on the 15-day injured list Sunday, a day after he exited following four batters and 12 pitches because of right lat tightness.

Hard-throwing right-hander Winston Santos was recalled from Triple-A Round Rock and joined the Rangers before the finale of their three-game series against the Toronto Blue Jays.

About an hour before the game, the Rangers said right fielder Brandon Nimmo was being scratched from the starting lineup because of illness.

Before the IL move was announced, manager Skip Schumaker said the Rangers knew going into Saturday night's game that Quantrill's velocity was lower.

Quantrill (9-5) was showing no signs of pain when Schumaker, pitching coach Jordan Tiegs and head trainer Matt Lucero went to the mound in the second inning and he came out of the game. Quantrill has a 2.86 ERA in 32 games (15 starts) after going to spring training with the Rangers on a minor league deal.

He left his previous start after six innings and 70 pitches at Arizona last Sunday with back soreness.

Quantrill, 31, has a 1.75 ERA (11 earned runs in 56⅔ innings) over his past 11 appearances (10 starts). Cam Schlittler of the New York Yankees at 1.64 is the only qualified pitcher with a better ERA over that span.

Santos is beginning his third stint with the Rangers, though his only appearance in the first two was his big league debut July 1 at Cleveland, where he allowed two runs in two innings. He has 103 strikeouts in 83⅓ innings in the minor leagues this season.

articles.headline: Gary Neville explains 'worst 15 minutes' Manchester United claim
articles.description: Gary Neville branded Manchester United's early second-half display against Fulham as the worst he had seen in more than 45 years.
articles.body:
Gary Neville branded Manchester United's early second-half display against Fulham as the worst he had seen in more than 45 years.

United were fortunate to leave Craven Cottage with a 1-1 draw after Matheus Cunha's late deflected effort snatched a point, but they had earlier gifted the hosts a comical own goal from Lisandro Martínez.

It came in the 63rd minute, capping a lethargic, error-strewn start to the half, and the goal felt fittingly surreal, Senne Lammens fumbling a tame shot with his legs and Martinez then tucked the ball past him as the goalkeeper struggled to find his balance.

During Sky Sports' coverage former United defender Neville described that period of the match as "absolutely pathetic."

"I've watched Man United since the age of five and that's the worst 15 minutes I've ever seen," Neville said.

"Absolutely pathetic. I've never seen such a lack of effort. What must [Michael] Carrick be thinking?"

Neville later explained his stance: "I was purely referring to the fact that they walked around the pitch. I have never seen Manchester United walk as much as that.

"Michael has got to stop defending them. I get why he's defending them, he is loyal and wants his players to work for him. There is a long way left in the season.

"I called them mannequins. I have never seen a Manchester United team, for 15 minutes, walk around as much as that. No alerts, not on your toes, you should always be on your toes, there was no shifting up two or three yards. Just walking when Fulham were in possession.

"There needs to be a rebalance. I wish he could play the attacking players but they are going to kill him defensively."

Neville added: "Not running is the only thing that I will call a disgrace."

- Man United rescue draw at Fulham after own goal shocker

- Fulham 1-1 Man United result: As it happened

A draw left United without a win in three Premier League games and means they will spend the international break in the bottom half of the table.

United made it their joint-lowest points return after five matches in the Premier League after failing to beat Fulham, previously set in 2014-15. That season under Louis van Gaal saw the team win only one of those opening five, 4-0 at home to QPR, although they recovered well and went on to finish fourth.

Press Association contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Packers WR Reed, RT Bako-Bewele carted off with injuries
articles.description: Packers wide receiver Jayden Reed and right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele were carted off the field on back-to-back plays.
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- Green Bay Packers wide receiver Jayden Reed was carted off the field after being placed on a stabilizing backboard with a neck injury following the second play from scrimmage in Sunday's game against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium.

On the very next play, Packers right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele sustained a right knee injury and also was carted off the field. Bako-Bewele's leg was immediately placed in a cast before he got on the cart.

Both players were quickly ruled out for the game by the Packers.

Members of the medical staff from both teams attended to Reed for several minutes on the field before he was placed on a board and had his helmet strapped down for stabilization.

Reed took what appeared to be a hit in the head and neck area at the end of a 4-yard gain on a swing pass in the left flat. Jets linebacker Demario Davis was the initial defender to hit Reed, and Kingsley Enagbare also may have made contact with Reed after that.

Players from both teams took a knee while Reed was down.

articles.headline: Premier League VAR review: Why no Man United penalty at Fulham?
articles.description: VAR often causes controversy, but how are decisions made? Our resident ref, Andy Davies, explains all.
articles.body:
The video assistant referee causes controversy every week, whether it be the Premier League, Champions League or FA Cup, but how are those decisions made and are they correct?

For the 2026-27 season, we are taking a look at the major incidents to explain the process in terms of both VAR protocol and the laws of the game. The most surprising, controversial and complicated decisions will be examined all season long right here.

 Andy Davies (@andydaviesref) is a former Select Group referee, with over 12 seasons on the elite list, working across the Premier League and Championship. With extensive experience at the elite level, he has operated within the VAR space in the Premier League and offers a unique insight into the processes, rationale and protocols that are delivered on a matchday. 

Should Man United have gotten a penalty at Fulham?

Fulham 1-1 Man United (Sept. 20)

Referee: Peter Bankes

VAR: Nick Hopton

Time: 86 minutes

Incident: Possible penalty to Man United for a handball

What happened: Man United's Lisandro Martínez felt he should have earned a penalty when he fired the ball at Fulham defender Calvin Bassey from close range and the ball struck Bassey's arm. The referee did not feel it was an offence and waved away the appeals for a penalty.

VAR decision: VAR agreed with the referee's interpretation of the incident, that the ball was struck at close range, defenders' arms were close to his body and within bodyline and therefore not a handball offence. VAR checked and cleared the on-filed decision as correct.

Verdict and insight: While Man United might have wanted the penalty, this was a correct on-field decision by the refereeing team and non-intervention by VAR.

This incident is a good example of how the handball law can create confusion in these types of situations. When the ball is struck at close range, the law is clear that the referee should allow play to continue if the player's hand or arm movement is the result of a natural reflex to potentially protect the player's face, and if such action does not make their body unnaturally bigger.

Additionally, if arms are within the body line and the ball would have struck the body/face this should also be taken into consideration when applying this law.

Bassey's reaction falls within this interpretation and was a good read by the on-field assistant referee, who would have led the communication in this incident.

Was Rice lucky not to be sent off at Brighton?

Brighton & Hove Albion 3-0 Arsenal (Sept. 19)

Referee: Darren England

VAR: Tim Wood

Time: 90 + 7 mins

Incident: Possible red card for Arsenal's Declan Rice

What happened: Rice picked up a late yellow card when he appeared to kick out at Brighton's Malick Yalcouyé in an off-the-ball incident.

VAR decision: The on-field decision of yellow card was checked and cleared as correct by the VAR.
